capability_summary: A single authoritative source of CircleTel's visual brand facts (logo variant system, colour palette with exact hex values, typography, clear-space and minimum-size rules) that is applied automatically whenever anything visual is produced for CircleTel — especially AI-generated imagery (product shots, social posts, hero backgrounds, icons, illustrations, mockups). It supplies the brand values to inject into any generation request, decides which logo file is correct for a given background and placement, sets output aspect/resolution expectations per asset type, and enforces that the real logo artwork is composited from files rather than synthesised by a model.
user_goal: The user wants every CircleTel-branded image or mockup that leaves this workspace to be unmistakably and correctly CircleTel — right orange, right secondary, right logo file for the background, real logo artwork (not an AI hallucination of it), professional and South-African-appropriate — without the user having to remember or re-state the brand values each time. The point is consistency across many assets produced by different people/tools on different days.
success_looks_like: Any generated CircleTel asset uses the brand colours by exact hex value, not by colour name, and a reviewer sampling the pixels finds the brand orange and secondary present and correct.
The logo appearing on a finished asset is the actual CircleTel logo artwork, pixel-identical to the supplied file — never a model's reconstruction of it.
The chosen logo variant is legible and correct for its background (light, dark, orange, print, small/email, social avatar) without the user having to say which file to use.
Clear space and minimum size around the logo are respected, so the mark is never crowded or rendered too small to read.
Asset dimensions/aspect ratio match the destination (square social, vertical story, wide hero/banner, 3:1 email header, square icon) on the first attempt.
The visual register is consistently modern, clean, professional, trustworthy and appropriate to the South African market — no clip-art, no neon, no busy compositions, no off-brand colours.
A second person can pick up the same brand facts later and produce an asset that sits beside the earlier one without a visible mismatch.
Finished assets land in a predictable, categorised location rather than scattered.
The brand values stated here agree with what the production website actually ships — a divergence between the guideline and the live product is a failure of this capability.

priority_qualities.quality: Factual exactness of the brand values (hex codes, logo file identity, typeface, clear space, minimum size)
priority_qualities.why_it_matters: This capability exists to be the source of truth. A wrong hex or a wrong logo variant is not a stylistic quibble — it produces off-brand collateral that may be printed, paid-promoted, or published. Every other quality is downstream of the numbers being right.

priority_qualities.quality: Logo integrity — the mark is never invented, distorted, or approximated
priority_qualities.why_it_matters: A logo is a fixed asset with legal and recognition value. Generative models reliably mangle it. The user has explicitly separated 'generate the scene' from 'place the real mark' to protect this.
A dark logo on a dark background or an orange logo on an orange field is invisible; the reason eight variants exist is so the right one is picked automatically rather than debated each time.
The user's stated value is that brand context is injected even for 'quick' one-off images. If it only applies when explicitly invoked, drift resumes immediately.

priority_qualities.quality: Fit-for-destination output (aspect ratio, resolution, file placement)
priority_qualities.why_it_matters: An asset with the wrong ratio must be regenerated or crops badly on the platform it was made for; wrong resolution fails in print. This is cheap to get right up front and expensive to fix later.
Colour alone does not make a coherent brand; a set of images that varies wildly in style still reads as inconsistent even when the hex codes match.

priority_qualities.quality: Local-market appropriateness (South African context, especially when depicting people or places)
priority_qualities.why_it_matters: The audience is South African; generic imported stock imagery undermines the 'local, trustworthy' positioning the brand is built on.
The user wants a check performed before an asset is considered finished, so errors are caught in-house rather than by a customer seeing the wrong orange.

constraints: Colours must be specified as exact hex values in any generation request; colour names alone are not acceptable.
Brand context must accompany every image request, including trivial or throwaway ones.
The logo must be composited from the stored artwork files after the image is generated; the generation step must be told to leave the logo out and, where relevant, to reserve space for it.
Logo variant must be chosen by background and placement, using the documented selection rules.
Clear space around the logo must equal the height of the 'TEL' wordmark element.
The logo must never be reproduced below 32px height for digital or 10mm for print.
Output aspect ratio and resolution must be selected to match the asset's destination before generating.
Generated assets must be filed into the designated categorised output tree, not left loose or in the project root.
People and settings depicted should read as South African where the asset shows lifestyle or human context.
A pre-release check must confirm correct primary colour, absence of off-brand colours, correct logo variant for the background, correct aspect ratio, professional aesthetic, and correct filing.
Aesthetic register is fixed: modern, clean, professional, uncluttered, trustworthy, innovative, approachable.
Typography in generated imagery should read as a clean sans-serif consistent with the brand's UI type.
Where a colour is used on an element, related shadows should be colour-matched to that element rather than defaulting to neutral black.
never_do: Never ask an image model to draw, render, recreate or 'faithfully reproduce' the CircleTel logo or wordmark — always composite the real file.
Never specify brand colour by name only ('orange', 'blue and orange') where a hex value is required.
Never skip brand context on the grounds that an image is quick, internal, or a draft.
Never use a logo variant whose colouring conflicts with its background (e.g. dark mark on dark field, orange mark on orange field).
Never introduce off-brand colours, neon palettes, or colours outside the defined primary/extended palette.
Never produce clip-art, cartoonish, or visually busy/cluttered compositions.
Never crowd the logo below the required clear space or scale it below the stated minimum size.
Never repurpose a reserved semantic colour (success/error/info, and the reserved messaging-channel green) for decorative use.
Never save generated assets to the project root or outside the designated asset tree.
Never publish an asset without running the pre-release brand check.
objective_invariants: PRIMARY COLOUR — CircleTel Orange, hex #F5831F, rgb(245, 131, 31). Token name in this skill: circleTel-orange. Used for primary brand presence, CTAs, highlights, accent lighting, price text. NOTE: this exact value is contested — see tensions; production Tailwind token circleTel.orange resolves to #E87A1E.

SECONDARY COLOUR — Dark Neutral / dark charcoal, hex #1F2937, rgb(31, 41, 55). Token name: circleTel-darkNeutral. Used for body text, headings, dark UI, illustration outlines. NOTE: contested — sibling image-generation skills and production DESIGN.md use Deep Navy #1B2A4A as the secondary; see tensions.
TERTIARY / BACKGROUND — Light Neutral, hex #E6E9EF, rgb(230, 233, 239). Token name: circleTel-lightNeutral. Used for backgrounds and cards, alongside plain white.
EXTENDED — Orange Light #FEF3E8 (hover states, light backgrounds).
EXTENDED — Orange Dark #D96F1A (pressed states, shadows).
EXTENDED — Gray #6B7280 (secondary text, borders, captions).
EXTENDED — Success Green #10B981 (success states, confirmations).
EXTENDED — Error Red #EF4444 (errors, warnings).
EXTENDED — Info Blue #3B82F6 (information, links).
SELECTED-STATE BLUE — #1E4B85, reserved for selected package-card states.

COLOUR USAGE RULES — Primary actions: #F5831F. Body text: #1F2937. Backgrounds: #E6E9EF or white. Accents: orange solid or orange gradient. Selected states: #1E4B85. Shadows: colour-matched to the element they sit under.

TYPOGRAPHY FONT STACK (as stated in this skill) — `font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;`. NOTE: contested — production ships Manrope (headings/display) + Inter (body/UI/data) + JetBrains Mono (mono); see tensions.
TYPOGRAPHY WEIGHTS — 600 semibold for subheadings and labels; 700 bold for headings and CTAs; 800 extrabold for hero text and major headlines.

TEXT STYLE SCALE — Hero headline 48–64px / weight 800 / Dark Neutral. Section heading 32–40px / 700 / Dark Neutral. Subheading 20–24px / 600 / Dark Neutral. Body 16px / 400 / Dark Neutral. Caption 14px / 400 / Gray. Price 24–32px / 700 / Orange.
LOGO SYSTEM — exactly 8 variants, stored as image files under a dedicated logo directory, filenames of the form `FLAT COLOUR - CIRCLE TEL LOGO-0N.png` where N is 1–8.
LOGO-01 — Orange + Gray on white/transparent. PRIMARY variant: website, documents, formal use, light backgrounds.
LOGO-02 — Orange only on white/transparent. Single-colour printing, embroidery.
LOGO-03 — Gray only on white/transparent. Neutral contexts, black-and-white documents.
LOGO-04 — Black only on white/transparent. High contrast, legal documents, stamps.
LOGO-05 — White only, transparent background. For DARK backgrounds and for placement over orange areas (knocked out).
LOGO-06 — White mark on an orange background block/square. Social avatars, app icons, favicons; also preferred for compositing onto dark or gradient backgrounds for high visibility.
LOGO-07 — Orange + Gray on white, small-size optimised. Email signatures, small placements.
LOGO-08 — Orange + Gray on white, large/high-resolution. Print, banners, billboards.

LOGO SELECTION RULES — dark or black background → LOGO-05; social avatar/icon → LOGO-06; print/large format → LOGO-08; email/small placement → LOGO-07; single-colour requirement → LOGO-02 (orange) or LOGO-03 (gray); formal/primary/default → LOGO-01. For compositing specifically: dark/gradient background → LOGO-06; light/white background → LOGO-01; over orange areas → LOGO-05; print/large → LOGO-08; small/email → LOGO-07.

LOGO ANATOMY — the mark comprises: (a) dual swirl circles, outer orange and inner gray, representing connectivity and dynamic service; (b) a WiFi signal icon integrated into the letter 'c', signalling wireless/internet focus; (c) the wordmark 'circle' set in lowercase orange followed by 'TEL' in uppercase bold gray. NOTE: contested — sibling skills describe the mark as a 'circle-and-arc motif'; see tensions.
LOGO CLEAR SPACE — maintain padding on all sides equal to the height of the 'TEL' wordmark element.
LOGO MINIMUM SIZE — 32px height for digital; 10mm height for print.
LOGO PROHIBITION — the logo must never be generated, drawn, or reconstructed by an image model; it is only ever composited from the stored artwork files.

DEFAULT COMPOSITING GEOMETRY — logo scaled to approximately 20% of the base image width (adjustable), positioned bottom-right by default, with padding of approximately 3% of the base image width from the edges; alpha-composited so transparency is preserved; final save at high quality.

ASSET TYPE MATRIX — Product: 1:1, 2K (2048x2048), normally no logo. Social Post: 1:1, 1K (1024x1024), LOGO-06 in a corner or LOGO-01. Social Story: 9:16, 2K (1152x2048), LOGO-06 top or bottom. Hero: 21:9, 2K–4K (2048x878), normally no logo (overlaid in code). Feature: 4:3, 1K (2048x1536), no logo. Icon: 1:1, 512x512, no logo. Banner: 21:9, 2K (2048x878), LOGO-01 or LOGO-05. Email Header: 3:1, 1K (1800x600), LOGO-01 or LOGO-07.

BRAND CONTEXT BLOCK (the exact substance to inject into any image request) — Primary colour: vibrant orange #F5831F. Secondary colour: dark charcoal #1F2937. Background: clean white or light gray #E6E9EF. Style: modern, professional, South African market. Mood: trustworthy, innovative, approachable. Typography: clean sans-serif. Avoid: overly busy designs, neon colours, clip-art style.

OUTPUT FILING — generated imagery is filed under a dedicated image tree with fixed categories: products (with per-product-type subfolders), sections (hero, features), marketing (social), icons (features), mockups. Prompt definitions are filed under a parallel prompts tree by category.

PRE-RELEASE CHECK — confirm: primary orange used correctly; no off-brand colours; logo variant appropriate for the background; clean professional aesthetic; South African market appropriate; correct aspect ratio for intended use; saved to the correct output subfolder.

Copywriting, campaign messaging strategy, and offer/pricing content.

Photo retouching, video, motion, and audio branding.

Accessibility contrast auditing of production interfaces.
Media buying, placement, and platform publishing.
Document/collateral templating (specs, one-pagers, battlecards) and the confidentiality rules that govern them.
